edge_sample.source_text: definition Simple Ring: A ring is simple if it has no nontrivial two-sided ideals.
edge_sample.target_text: theorem : A simple ring is prime.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Set of Matrix Units: A set $e_{ij}$ for $i, j \in [1, n]$ is a \textit{set of matrix units} of $R$ if $$ e_{ij}e_{kl} = \begin{cases} e_{il} & \mid j = k \\ 0 & \mid \text{otherwise}\end{cases} $$ and $\sum_{i=1}^n e_{ii} = 1$.
definition Corner Ring Set: The set of the corner ring is $eRe$.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Left/Right Ideal: A \textit{left/right ideal} $I$ of a ring $R$ is an additive subgroup of $R$ such that $rI \subseteq I$ for all $r \in R$ or $Ir \subseteq I$ for all $r \in R$, respectively.
edge_sample.target_text: theorem : Let $R$ be a semisimple ring. Then, $R$ is isomorphic to a direct product of simple, artinian rings.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Left/Right Ideal: A \textit{left/right ideal} $I$ of a ring $R$ is an additive subgroup of $R$ such that $rI \subseteq I$ for all $r \in R$ or $Ir \subseteq I$ for all $r \in R$, respectively.
edge_sample.target_text: theorem : If $e, f \in R$ are orthogonal idempotents and $f \neq 0$, then the left ideal generated by $1 - e - f$ is strictly smaller than the left ideal generated by $1 - e$.

edge_sample.source_text: definition Two-sided Ideal: A two-sided ideal is a subset of $R$ that is both left and right ideal of $R$.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : Suppose $x \in I J$. Then $x \in I$ since $I$ is a twosided ideal. Also $x \in J$ since $J$ is a left ideal. But then $x = 0$ since $I \cap J = 0$.
